title: Inspect and extend: Keep a last-known view when storage or network fails
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/store.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve cache keys, load/save, corrupt data, provider startup, and fallback state.
problem: A cache is a last-known copy, not the source of truth. Follow provider initialization and storage fallbacks, then inspect tests for malformed JSON and a failing backend. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/store.ts` and the related project files: src/store.ts; src/githubContext.tsx; test/github.test.ts.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to cache keys, load/save, corrupt data, provider startup, and fallback state.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Cached repository/issue data can be stale and is not evidence of a current provider response.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A cache is a last-known copy, not the source of truth. Follow provider initialization and storage fallbacks, then inspect tests for malformed JSON and a failing backend.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/store.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
